title: Filter invoices by an amount sent as a string

conversation.text: Manual workflow: GET the invoices from https://api.example.com/invoices (no auth). It returns a list of invoices, each with an id and an amount. Note: the API returns amount as a string, e.g. "120.50". Keep only the invoices with an amount greater than 100 and POST each one as JSON {"id": <invoice id>, "amount": <amount as a number>} to https://hooks.example.com/large-invoices. Drop the invoices of 100 or less.

description: The IF and Filter nodes validate types strictly by default, so a number comparison on a string amount throws. Grades that only the invoice above 100 passes the IF or Filter node, run by its own code, and that the POST sends amount as a number.

executionScenarios.name: large-invoices-posted-with-number-amount
executionScenarios.description: The IF and Filter nodes validate types strictly by default, so a number comparison on a string amount throws.
executionScenarios.dataSetup: GET https://api.example.com/invoices returns 200 [{ "id": "i1", "amount": "120.50" }, { "id": "i2", "amount": "80.00" }, { "id": "i3", "amount": "100" }]. The hooks endpoint returns 200 { "ok": true } for any POST.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: Exactly one POST reaches https://hooks.example.com/large-invoices with body { "id": "i1", "amount": 120.5 }, with amount a number. A type validation error, a POST for i2 or i3, or amount as the string '120.50' FAIL.

outcomeExpectations: The workflow converts amount to a number (or enables loose type validation) before the greater-than-100 comparison, sends only i1 on the true branch, and posts amount as a number.
